# Reviewer application

**Stellar Discovery Trust Layer — TokenJunkieLabs — SCF #46 Build / Open Track**

## Project and requested outcome

TokenJunkieLabs is building open-source, self-hostable software for selling and using paid APIs, datasets and agent tools on Stellar. A merchant chooses a resource and its terms. A buyer approves a specific request, controls its wallet and spending, and receives the complete result in its existing application. The software connects that agreement to native settlement, delivery, fulfillment and recovery, so another engineer can take over the working service.

We request **USD 38,000 for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from actual award acceptance**. The funded outcome is **two independently operated merchants, two independent buyer operators, and the same useful service operating through two independently operated facilitators**. Delivery progresses from installed customer services to recurring testnet use, mainnet use and an independent maintainer’s recovery and handover.

The existing product supplies the architecture, merchant and buyer workspaces, source adapters, payment integration and complete-result receiving. The grant funds the remaining engineering against the selected customers’ actual sources, applications and hosts: customer-specific integration, provider registration, deployed threat response, production release, material defects and technical receiving. Its six priced deliverables appear below.

## Customer problem, need and adoption

A paid endpoint is useful when its output completes a customer’s task. An analyst may need every page of a dataset, the full filing comparison or a newly reviewed reporting period. An agent application may need a query result in its existing typed client. A merchant also needs to know which approved request was paid, what was delivered and whether the required order or accounting action finished.

Those jobs join four records: **the approved request, settled transfer, complete output and accepted fulfillment or accounting**. A task may require several priced requests, so the buyer needs its aggregate cost and complete output together. Staff must also recover an interrupted request and transfer the installed service to another maintainer.

Current human conversations give us specific customer learning:

|CoCart|Founder Sébastien Dumont asked about introductions, the payer, referral compensation, responsibilities and contracting.|One customer’s headless cart, native WooCommerce checkout, payment/order operation and receiving; proposed $7,200 for 60 hours over fifteen business days.|
|Blockscout|Mojmir Racak expressed interest on October 12 and reported no current integration budget.|One approved PRO API token-information operation, buyer integration and handover; proposed $4,800 over ten business days.|


These are proposed workshares and observed conversations. The commissioning agreement and funded customer cohort remain to be selected. A source platform, its merchant operator and the customer funding implementation can be different organizations. CoCart’s questions, for example, require an explicit choice of the first merchant or agency and the commissioning arrangement. Bryce owns these relationships and subsequent agreements.

Each selected installation uses an original workorder naming the payer, merchant, independent buyer and receiving engineer. It defines the authorized source and access, exact operation, complete useful output, priced unit, host, receiving application and delivery acceptance. It also identifies the reason for a later purchase: a fresh period, changed source edition or distinct customer request. The same task then proceeds through installation, native payment, complete receiving, recurring use and handover.

The existing commercial model supports this adoption path: fixed-fee implementation of an agreed customer operation, followed by separately scoped care. A customer commissions the source and application adaptation; the merchant retains its resource receipts; TokenJunkieLabs invoices its agreed engineering and handover. Actual acceptance, implementation effort, corrections, support demand and collections inform following offers.

## Why Stellar and what we contribute

Stellar settles the operation the buyer approved. The approval binds the request to its network, asset, recipient and integer atomic amount. The native Stellar SDK and selected payment service verify and settle the authorization; the application connects that outcome to the original source, useful result and merchant fulfillment. Buyers retain signing and aggregate spending authority. Merchants retain control of their resources, terms and order actions.

We compose existing ecosystem infrastructure. The x402 Exact Stellar scheme and facilitator supply payment verification and settlement. Vellar’s optional discovery extension publishes eligible settled resources to its catalogue. OpenZeppelin, Veridex and Periplo supply relevant payment infrastructure, while Rumble Fish is developing facilitator, discovery and SDK capabilities. The existing MPP Charge workbench retains its own challenge, authorization and recovery model. The implementation uses existing SDKs and token contracts.

**Business and technical market comparison — October 12, 2026.** The closest products already make substantial parts of a paid Stellar service possible. The comparison below identifies the existing capability and the customer work our award must deliver around it.

**Business value and adoption.** The first customer is an organization commissioning a repeatable information or application operation: for example, a complete filing comparison, reviewed laboratory delivery or recurring economic report. Its workorder names the commissioning payer, resource merchant, independent buyer and receiving engineer, with one agreed output and acceptance procedure. TokenJunkieLabs earns the fixed implementation fee and separately scoped care; the merchant retains its resource receipts. Selection favors a real reason for repeat use, an authorized source, a customer application that can receive the result and a maintainer who can operate the installation. The existing conversation records and delivery examples inform that selection.

**Technical improvement to be delivered.** The reusable product joins the original source, approved request and terms, native transfer, complete usable result and required fulfillment in one continuing customer operation. For a paginated dataset that includes its whole selected population; for a file or report it includes the complete bytes and the source edition used to produce them. An interrupted request reopens with its original financial and delivery state. Another authorized engineer receives the working configuration, decisions, history and customer files and completes the same task on the receiving host.

The six funded packages apply that architecture to the selected customers. T1 completes both source/application adaptations and a second operator’s handover. T2 operates the same useful service through two facilitators and completes the installed recovery cases. T3 establishes recurring mainnet use, restores the production state and completes independent maintenance. These are the proposed improvements reviewers can evaluate: useful customer output, repeat independent purchases, preserved operation when the payment provider changes and an installation another engineer can maintain.

Our contribution is the reusable operation around those payment components: preserve source meaning and pagination, review exact requests and terms, acquire the complete result, receive it into an existing application or workbook, and reopen the service after interruption or on another authorized host. That gives a Stellar merchant a path from a paid endpoint to an independently maintainable customer installation.

A retained comparison found 27 Vellar offers and two Periplo offers with no shared seller/route identity. The two-facilitator deliverable therefore includes actual registration and integration of the **same useful service** with both operators. Its completion must preserve the customer operation when payment infrastructure changes. Reusable integration, receiving and operating improvements return to the public source.

## Defined architecture and operating behavior

The system has six components: the merchant’s private source/release workspace; its public HTTP or MCP operation; the native Stellar SDK and facilitator; the buyer’s private approval and spending state; complete-result and delivery records; and merchant fulfillment/accounting. Node.js supplies merchant and buyer interfaces. Source adapters and receiving applications retain their own native data and operating semantics.

|Stage|Implemented behavior|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|Review and publish|The merchant selects a source edition or named live query, request schema, output, limits and resolved payment options. Review includes source rights, route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Source or terms changes become later reviewed states.|
|Connect the source|Adapters preserve types, missing and null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select authorized access. The output identifies its source edition.|
|Approve and purchase|The buyer retains the endpoint, method or MCP tool, arguments, selected terms and scope. The remote schema and challenge must match before signing. Per-payment limits and the application’s existing reservation/budget owner govern spending.|
|Settle and deliver|The facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. The application retains the server outcome, complete output and durable merchant notification. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the transaction’s network, asset, parties and atomic amount.|
|Use and continue|The receiving application opens all pages and files required by the task. A parent acquisition retains its priced requests and unfinished coverage. Earlier acquired output remains available when a later source edition changes.|
|Operate and hand over|The customer selects its release, HTTPS service, restricted administration and supervision. A receiving engineer can drain, restart, roll back and restore the installation with its operating history and complete customer files.|


For paid MCP, the HTTP endpoint, tool and arguments are retained separately from the payment resource. An unsigned call obtains the challenge. Its full payment option, including authorization timeout, must match the saved quote before the buyer retains dispatch state and sends the signed call. The official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata. HTTP operations use the native HTTP transport.

Recovery keeps server confirmation, independently observed transfer, complete output, receiver acknowledgment and fulfillment separately visible. An uncertain signed response stays attached to its original dispatch for reconciliation. Reopening an acquired result uses saved work; unfinished delivery continues from its original intent. A changed request or new purchase receives a new review.

Browser, terminal, typed clients and MCP operate the same retained workspaces. Customer exports include configuration selection, history and all referenced files. The receiving host supplies current authorized secret references. Buyer accounting also carries reviewed expense and credit allocations into connected QuickBooks and Xero accounts, with review of changed charts, affected mappings and journal lines before application.

The merchant financial workspace carries that paid operation into its original settlement accounting and customer records. Issued service invoices retain exact amounts and billing identity; actual receipts, dated allocations and credits determine the balance. Reviewed installment plans distribute that balance across due dates and preserve every customer edition. The Xero handover maps issued invoices and credits to the receiving organisation's original templates, retains returned document IDs and exact amounts, and continues corrections through the same package family. Native network, asset and atomic amount remain attached to the original settlement; commercial valuations retain their explicit basis. The receiving engineer can reopen the complete workspace, customer files and financial history and continue the same task.

## Working product and demonstrated results

The retained network register contains **18 distinct team-operated development purchases totaling 411,000 stroops, or 0.0411 native testnet XLM**, with fees tracked separately. Each connects its original transaction to the complete output. The funded milestones apply this working foundation to independent merchant and buyer operators.

Three completed operations show the customer result:

|Operation|Completed result|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|Municipal data|A Queens HPD source contained 1,342 building-in-project rows. The selected output received all 144 rows in paid pages of 100 and 44. Both 10,000-stroop transfers finalized. The complete CSV/JSONL edition reopened with its source and accounting.|
|Paid agent query|The MariaDB HPD Preservation/minimum-20 query returned all 100 rows,14 columns and 53,468 bytes for one 50,000-stroop purchase. Scalar strings and the declared truncation indicator were retained. The purchase reopened with signing disconnected, and the complete result reopened in another directory.|
|Filing analysis|A 10,000-stroop purchase delivered the Genpact 2024–2025 comparison: four disclosure pairs, five findings and all 1,027,807 bytes. The editable analyst workspace reopened it; repeat receipt preserved its revision; backup/restore reproduced the comparison in another installation.|


These operations demonstrate the common path from exact source/query selection through payment to a complete result that another operator can use. For recurring use, the paid operation can deliver a new reporting period, source release or customer query through that same path.

The prepaid API product extends it to allowances. Its completed example bought an eight-unit plan for 10,000 testnet stroops. An analysis of 2,4,6 and 8 with a two-value window returned the complete 279-byte result, including count 4, sum 20, mean 5 and window means 2, 3, 5 and 7. The request consumed two units once; reopening retained six available. Merchant recovery preserved the application result, order, allowance and settlement outbox. The same funded workspace has now completed its ten merchant stages and all eight agent stages through the registered 33-tool provider and typed client. Its encrypted backup resumed from 4,096 bytes to the complete 144,771 bytes after the console closed; three exports comprising five files, the restored workspace and the original result reopened offline. The complete source and operating package contains all 25 delivery files.

Complete receiving also operates across source-specific customer applications. A Census workbook retained all sixteen rows across CSV, JSONL, SQLite, browser and Rust clients; a later edition identified fifteen unchanged rows and one changed row while the earlier customer retained its original values. The supplier workflow imported both complete 106-material SAP SHINE editions, reviewed their supplier changes and reopened the full catalogue handover. An installed incident-to-case operation completed an observation gap, notification retry, acknowledgment, recovery and support-case reopening.

**Gravity referral receiving.** Nine native phases completed from published Gravity 3.0.0 originals: complete referral/source review, one conditional HTTP update and readback, original status history, a changed Task dataset edition, CHALLENGE_ONLY merchant-edition and buyer-configuration reopen, and fresh whole-workspace restoration. This foundation supports an authorised referral quality or closure analysis, or an agreed source-data query. Commissioning names the source edition, returned result, price, merchant, payer and independent buyer and receiving operators, and assigns the installation work to the existing six funded packages. [Complete operating result and receiving guide](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/commons/blob/732163f1642772d130e5e21d1c919be89582b730/tools/revenue_owner_console_20261010/case_assets/elimu-gravity-referral-implementation-20261012-450e/OPERATED_GRAVITY_RECEIVING.md).

The captioned 3-minute-32-second product/team film follows a native HPD query, saved terms, one 0.005-testnet-XLM purchase, complete result, download and reopening. Its editable companion contains the clips, captions, script, result and rendering tools. The reviewer workbench completed full-result receiving, export, cold reopening and second-operator receiving on desktop and 390-pixel mobile views. The merchant Customers workspace retains the complete customer packet, source documents, saved results and receiving files through its delivery and recovery operations.

The original merchant accounting exercise also completed invoice issue, credit, receipt allocation, Xero-format JSON receiving, document-ID conflict correction, full handover export and cold reopening at revision 23. Its two invoice records, one credit and two linked package generations remained available with their original files. This completes the financial handover foundation used by the selected merchant installations.

## Threat response and outcome measurement

The T2 threat model and monitoring plan are part of the 50-hour/$4,750 deployed-response package. Each installation records its source edition, merchant/buyer authority, network and facilitator, protected records, reviewed thresholds, notification destinations and named primary/backup responders.

The plan connects the actual threats to observations and permitted responses: changed offers or approvals; incorrect financial or output attribution; unauthorized authority or access; interrupted delivery; lost monitoring; and restoration of the wrong generation. A confirmed integrity contradiction opens an incident. Age, rate and capacity thresholds use the installation’s reviewed values.

Acceptance operates two cases against the deployed service: an interrupted settled purchase and a merchant-delivery failure. Their records retain the actual notification and acknowledgment, financial and delivery outcomes, response and recovery times, material remediation or residual findings, and the receiving engineer’s same-case reopening after drain/restart. An uncertain payment is reconciled through its original intent. A coverage gap remains visible until observation resumes.

A completed purchase joins a distinct approved intent, an independently observed native transfer and complete useful output. Native transactions are counted once within each network. Independent organizations or people are counted once across their agents and wallets. A returning buyer’s distinct completed purchase increases purchases without adding a buyer; reopening an acquired result or resuming its download continues the original purchase.

Cohort reporting includes completed/attempted purchases, complete/started parent datasets or files, returning buyers, accepted handovers and partial, unresolved, canceled and refunded outcomes. Required fulfillment remains separately visible. This makes the funded targets assessable against the whole observation window.

For each installation, we record the customer’s existing task and, where available, its prior active effort, manual corrections and time to useful output. Comparison uses the same input/output definition and source population or period. Customer acceptance and unresolved corrections accompany the measurements. The practical value is usable output, less manual work, recurring demand and a service the customer’s engineer can maintain.

## Delivery capacity, payment timing and sustainability

The four SCF payments would be **$3,800 at award acceptance, followed by $7,600,$11,400 and $15,200 after the respective milestone approvals**. These payments differ from the costs of completing each tranche. The request is denominated in USD-equivalent value and paid in XLM, using the settlement-price mechanism in SCF’s Official Rules §5.6.

The complete resource study retains all six packages, their dependencies,400 hours and $38,000. With an illustrative December 7, 2026 start and its explicit working-day calendar, **25 engineering plus eight integration/handover hours per week** is the lowest examined timely allocation. T1 finishes January 6 and final handover April 13, ahead of the illustrative May 6 day-150 target. The awarded schedule will use the actual acceptance date, named contributors and their working availability.

Under the selected schedule’s labor-accrual assumptions, the modeled peak additional cash requirement is **$17,250 with a 14-day review/payment lag,$23,275 at 30 days and $26,600 at 60 days**. Opening cash is currently unentered. Actual contributor payment dates, commitments, agreed deferrals and received funds must be recorded in that same operating case. The forecast quantifies what those arrangements need to cover; commercial proposals retain their own assignments, stages and collections.

Each tranche completion form is due within 90 calendar days of receiving the previous tranche payment. Actual receipt dates determine those form deadlines; the 150-day delivery plan begins at award acceptance. The grant case retains the deliverables, submissions, payments and any SCF-confirmed schedule amendment.

Sustainability comes from reusable open-source installation and receiving capabilities, paid customer-specific implementation, and separately scoped care. The original commercial workorder records delivery effort, included corrections, support responsibilities, acceptance and collections. Grant-funded reusable Stellar work and separately commissioned integration are assigned once. Additional reusable work completed before award is removed from the remaining grant estimate.
